copy.blurb:
The model fancies the draw more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against Haiti. +4.2pp is a narrow gap; that's what fires this as a Pick on the draw side.

On Elo, Brazil comes in 520 points ahead — Brazil at 1970, Haiti at 1450. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Brazil to win at 86%, the draw at 10%, and Haiti to win at 4%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. the draw on the win side reads 10%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Brazil to win at 92%, the draw at 6%, and Haiti to win at 3%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the the draw side — 6% on the market, 10% on the engine, a +4.2pp gap.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the the draw side that lower bound is 10% — +4.2pp clear of the market's 6%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The engine isn't arguing reputation, recency, or narrative. It's reading the underlying numbers and finding the draw priced shorter on the market than the prior supports — that's the disagreement.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 29 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call. Per The Guardian (football): "He will be an important player in this World Cup." drivers: Pre-match Elo gives the draw a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +4.2pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
This is a selection call on the the draw side, not a blanket read on the market.
Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.

copy.summary: The model and the market disagree on whether a stalemate is in play here. Our prior puts the draw at 10%; Polymarket prices it at 6%. The +4.2pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Brazil v Haiti · the model leans the draw
